Key Research Thinking Patterns: Quantum Confinement Engineering for Optoelectronic Optimization: Utilizing Schrödinger equation solutions and density of states calculations to design multiple quantum well (MQW) structures that manipulate L-valley degeneracy and strain effects, thereby enhancing internal quantum efficiency and power density in IV-VI semiconductors (e.g., modeling Pb0.81Sn0.19Se/Pb0.80Sr0.20Se MQWs to achieve a 49% power density improvement over bulk materials).

Thermodynamic-Electrical Co-Optimization for System-Level Viability: Integrating radiative heat transfer analysis with electrical power generation density calculations to evaluate the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) of hybrid systems, ensuring that device-level performance translates into competitive grid-scale economics (e.g., demonstrating that TPV systems coupled with molten silicon thermal storage can achieve energy costs below $0.10/kWh).

Current-Density Matching and Junction Architecture Analysis: Applying dual-junction device simulation and current density matching optimization to determine the optimal number of junctions and layer thicknesses for specific thermal radiator temperatures, balancing efficiency gains against manufacturing complexity (e.g., analyzing the trade-off where current-matched dual-junction designs at 1400°C yielded lower efficiency than single-junction counterparts for specific PbSe-based alloys).

Spectroscopic Metabolic Profiling for Biological Validation: Employing mid-infrared laser absorption spectroscopy with interband cascade lasers (ICL) and lock-in amplification to detect volatile metabolic biomarkers in real-time, correlating gas-phase concentrations with cellular physiological states (e.g., using acetaldehyde detection in headspace gas to distinguish hypoxic from normoxic breast cancer cell cultures with a 37 ppb detection limit).
Summary Description: Patrick McCann is a researcher specializing in the intersection of semiconductor physics, thermophotovoltaics (TPV), and biophotonics. His primary focus is the development of low-cost, high-efficiency TPV systems for grid-scale thermal energy storage, utilizing IV-VI semiconductor multiple quantum well (MQW) structures such as PbSnSe/PbSrSe. He employs rigorous quantum confinement modeling, including Schrödinger equation solutions and density of states analysis, to optimize device performance and manufacturing viability on silicon substrates. Additionally, McCann applies mid-infrared laser absorption spectroscopy using interband cascade lasers to monitor metabolic biomarkers in cancer cell cultures, providing non-invasive tools for hypoxia research and cancer therapy monitoring. His work bridges fundamental materials science with translational applications in renewable energy infrastructure and precision oncology.
